title: Compatible finite-free models for inverse-ring reconstruction
statement: For a tower of commutative rings with surjective nilpotent transitions and compatible derived objects satisfying the marked lifting [lem-weil-pbc-nilpotent-marked-free-complex-lift], tower limit [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-module-complex-tower-limit], K-flat scalar extension [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], and coefficient adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] hypotheses, there exist bounded-above finite-free complexes, surjective transitions, a termwise limit complex, markings, projections, scalar-extension isomorphisms, and all corresponding chain-level compatibility equations.

source.place: Tag 0CQF, compatible finite-free model construction and projection calculations

proof.text: Normalize the supplied derived adjunctions using the universal derived scalar extension of modules, preservation of right Kan extensions by a right adjoint, and uniqueness of left adjoints. This gives a universal counit whose adjoint is the ordinary scalar-extension unit.

Apply nilpotent invariance to propagate pseudo-coherence from level zero. Transport marked finite-free lifting along the quotient ring isomorphism and inductively choose bounded-above finite-free models with one common cutoff, together with marked transition isomorphisms. Their adjoints are surjective in every degree.

Lift a fixed finite basis through each transition. Nilpotent Nakayama makes the lifted basis map surjective; an arbitrary finite-free basis and the Orzech property make it injective. Compatible basis coordinates and the stated universal property of A identify the module of compatible tuples with a finite power of A. This argument also handles zero rings and the empty basis.

Construct the complex of compatible tuples with coordinatewise differential, and its evaluation projections. These form a limit cone. The compatible bases give finite freeness of every term and prove that the adjoint scalar extensions of the projections are isomorphisms. The common upper cutoff holds coordinatewise.

Use the surjective-tower kernel/one-minus-shift short exact sequence and exact countable products to obtain a derived-limit triangle in the chosen derived-category universe. Invert the stipulated restriction-composition compatibility equation and use naturality to identify its marked transition maps with those of E. A product isomorphism and the triangulated-category comparison axiom give beta with the required projection equations.

The normalized universal scalar-extension counit is invertible on the bounded-above finite-free limit complex, by the bounded-flat computation reused from nilpotent invariance. Use this counit as gamma and the ordinary adjunction unit as eta. Apply the derived adjunction bijection and the projection equations to prove the last comparison identity; the component unit and projection identities follow from the chain adjunction.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0CQF; compatible basis construction and normalized adjunction comparison, G3

theorem reconstruction_models :
    ∃ (Pₙ : ∀ n, CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} (R n)) ℤ)
      (b : ℤ) (βₙ : ∀ n, Q.obj (Pₙ n) ≅ Eₙ n)
      (uₙ : ∀ n, Pₙ (n + 1) ⟶
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (φ n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj (Pₙ n))
      (θₙ : ∀ n, ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (φ n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
        (Pₙ (n + 1)) ≅ Pₙ n)
      (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) ℤ) (β : Q.obj P ≅ E)
      (p : ∀ n, P ⟶
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj (Pₙ n))
      (θ : ∀ n, ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (q n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P ≅ Pₙ n)
      (η : ∀ n, P ⟶ ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
        (((ModuleCat.extendScalars (q n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P))
      (γ : ∀ n, (M n).obj (Q.obj P) ≅
        Q.obj (((ModuleCat.extendScalars (q n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)),
      (∀ n, (Pₙ n).IsStrictlyLE b) ∧
      (∀ n i, Module.Free (R n) ((Pₙ n).X i) ∧ Module.Finite (R n) ((Pₙ n).X i)) ∧
      (∀ n i, Function.Surjective ((uₙ n).f i)) ∧
      (∀ n i, ((ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj (φ n)).homEquiv
        ((Pₙ (n + 1)).X i) ((Pₙ n).X i) ((θₙ n).hom.f i)) = (uₙ n).f i) ∧
      (∀ n, Q.map (uₙ n) = (βₙ (n + 1)).hom ≫ t n ≫
        (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (φ n)).mapDerivedCategory.map (βₙ n).inv ≫
        (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (φ n)).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app (Pₙ n)) ∧
      P.IsStrictlyLE b ∧
      (∀ i, Module.Free A (P.X i) ∧ Module.Finite A (P.X i)) ∧
      (∀ n i (y : P.X i), (uₙ n).f i ((p (n + 1)).f i y) = (p n).f i y) ∧
      (∀ i (x : ∀ n, (Pₙ n).X i), (∀ n, (uₙ n).f i (x (n + 1)) = x n) →
        ∃! y : P.X i, ∀ n, (p n).f i y = x n) ∧
      (∀ n, Q.map (p n) ≫
        (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q n)).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app (Pₙ n) ≫
        (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q n)).mapDerivedCategory.map (βₙ n).hom =
        β.hom ≫ pE ≫ Pi.π _ n) ∧
      (∀ n i, ((ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj (q n)).homEquiv
        (P.X i) ((Pₙ n).X i) ((θ n).hom.f i)) = (p n).f i) ∧
      (∀ n i, (η n).f i = (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj (q n)).unit.app (P.X i)) ∧
      (∀ n, (adjq n).unit.app (Q.obj P) ≫
        (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q n)).mapDerivedCategory.map (γ n).hom ≫
        (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q n)).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app
          (((ModuleCat.extendScalars (q n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) =
        Q.map (η n)) ∧
      (∀ n, (γ n).hom ≫ Q.map (θ n).hom ≫ (βₙ n).hom =
        (M n).map β.hom ≫ ((adjq n).homEquiv E (Eₙ n)).symm (pE ≫ Pi.π _ n))
